item.title: UK order books open for refreshed electric Volvos
item.dc:creator: guest author
item.description: Volvo Car UK has just launched the refreshed 40 series range, now available for order in the UK. On-the-road prices start at £43,860 for the EX40 and £45,860 for the EC40.

item.title: Northumberland to sport 36 more public charge points
item.dc:creator: guest author
item.description: A new suite of electric vehicle chargers is being added to Northumberland County Council's existing network. The Council has passed a motion to add an additional 36 EV charging points at 26 locations. The picturesque coastal region in the Northeast of England, borders Scotland and is famous for being home to Hadrian's wall and the Northumberland National Park.

item.title: Norwegian operator Torghatten Nord takes delivery of electric ferry Misterøy
item.dc:creator: Florian Treiss
item.description: Norwegian shipping company Torghatten Nord from Tromsø has taken delivery of its new electric ferry named Misterøy. The nearly 77-meter-long Ro-Pax vessel was built at a Turkish shipyard and can transport up to 60 cars and 195 passengers. Two sister ships are set to follow.

item.title: BMW i3 completes North Cape to Tarifa journey with less than three hours of charging time
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: BMW completed a nearly 5,900-kilometer journey from the North Cape to Tarifa with the new i3 50 xDrive. According to the manufacturer, the electric 3-series required a total of only 2 hours and 46 minutes for recharging.

item.title: Confusion over continued production of the VW ID.3 in Zwickau, Germany
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: The ID.3 will also be built exclusively in Volkswagen's Zwickau plant in 2027, with the exception of the GTI variant, according to a statement made by Volkswagen’s Deputy Works Council Chairman Jürgen Mahnkopf yesterday at an automotive congress in Zwickau. Despite the worker's organisation's statment, the spokesperson for Volkswagen Sachsen has now denied the claim — and has made a point of emphasizing that ID.3 producton will move to the German carmaking giant's home of Wolfsburg next year.

item.title: ACEA Statistics show electric vans gain ground in EU
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: The European van market is stagnating, but plug-in models are gaining significant ground. In the first nine months of 2026, their new registrations in the EU increased by 38.2 percent to nearly 152,000 vehicles.

item.title: DPD UK expands electric fleet with 381 new Fords from November
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: DPD UK is further expanding its electric fleet. After 341 new Mercedes-Benz eSprinters already entered service with the delivery company in September 2026, DPD UK has now also ordered 381 Ford E-Transits. The electric vans are expected to be deployed starting mid-November.

item.title: Verne robotaxi service prepares for launch in Berlin
item.dc:creator: Florian Treiss
item.description: Robotaxi provider Verne is preparing to launch in Germany, starting with the capital. The Croatian company told electrive that it is building its operational presence in the country. Two job postings for the Berlin location provide clues about the structures it intends to establish. Verne has not yet announced a specific launch date.

item.title: Mercedes-Benz high-power charging gains traction in the USA
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: For its third anniversary in the USA, Mercedes-Benz High-Power Charging has taken stock. Within 36 months, the German automaker's infrastructure grew from a handful of test stations to a charging network of 100 locations and 934 charging points with a total of 245,000 customers.

item.title: Driventic refurbs London old-timer electric double-decker bus drivetrains
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: In London, 28 aging electric double-deckers are being comprehensively refurbished. The electric old-timers will receive new batteries and electric drives. The latter are being supplied by the German drivetrain specialist Driventic. After modernization, the electric double-deckers are set to return to service with the transport company Metroline.

item.title: Orders open for the Genesis GV90 in South Korea
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: Genesis is opening order books in South Korea for the GV90, its electric flagship. The highlight of the lineup is the four-seat Neolun variant, featuring all available equipment options, including the VIP package and underfloor heating, starting at approximately €165,600. The market launch in Europe is planned for the first half of 2027.

item.title: China’s electric car exports surge by 140%
item.dc:creator: Florian Treiss
item.description: Electric vehicles and plug-in hybrids manufactured in China are increasingly becoming an export hit for the People's Republic: In October alone, 606,000 plug-in vehicles were exported from the country — an increase of 140%. In contrast, domestic sales in China declined by 8.6%.

item.title: Kia invests billions in electric and PBV Centre
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: Kia plans to gradually transform the Autoland Gwangju plant into a modern hub for electric and autonomous vehicles by 2029, investing billions. The goal is to establish an industrial ecosystem for the development of modular electric vehicles, which Kia calls PBV - standing for "platform beyond vehicle" and simultaneously the anacronym for Purpose Built Vehicles (PBVs), in collaboration with the region and local universities.

item.title: Tozero announces first delivery of recycled lithium carbonate to customers
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: The German lithium-ion battery recycling startup Tozero has delivered its first recycled lithium carbonate to an industrial customer, Botz GmbH. The material was produced at Tozero's new demonstration plant in the Gendorf Chemical Park near Munich.

item.title: German study compares electric motors from China, Europe and the USA
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: Researchers at Germany's renown RWTH Aachen University examined 115 electric motors from 80 electric vehicles. They found that drivetrains from China, Europe, and the USA differ little in their basic design but vary in materials and individual construction details.

item.title: BYD combines solar arrays, energy storage and megawatt charging
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: BYD has unveiled a charging system in the Abu Dhabi desert that combines photovoltaics, battery storage, FLASH Charging, and a charging robot. According to CarNewsChina, the system achieved a charging power of 1,000 kW during a demonstration.

item.title: Mercedes discontinues EQE, EQE SUV and EQS SUV
item.dc:creator: Florian Treiss
item.description: The EQE sedan, EQE SUV, and EQS SUV are no longer individually configurable at Mercedes-Benz. This leaves only the EQS sedan remaining from the four large electric models based on the EVA-II platform, while a fully electric E-Class as an EQE alternative has already been announced for 2027.

item.title: California reopens $55m funding programme for electric school buses
item.dc:creator: Ciaran Daly
item.description: California has reopened its Zero-Emission School Bus and Infrastructure (ZESBI) incentive programme, with at least $55 million in state funding available to help school districts purchase electric school buses and install the associated charging infrastrcture.

item.title: India: ChargeZone announces 1,000 new DC fast-charging sites
item.dc:creator: Sagar Parikh
item.description: Indian EV charging service provider ChargeZone has announced plans to deploy DC fast chargers across 1,000 new locations in the country. The company says these chargers will serve both passenger and commercial electric vehicles.

item.title: Zenobe to finance 169 electric buses for Transport UK in London
item.dc:creator: Ciaran Daly
item.description: Zenobē has agreed to finance 169 battery-electric buses for Transport UK, alongside the development of charging infrastructure at four of the operator's London depots. The deal extends an existing partnership between the two companies and supports Transport UK's ambition to fully electrify its London bus fleet by 2030.

item.title: Infineon processes SiC on 300 mm wafers for the first time
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: Infineon has produced the first functional SiC power devices on 300-millimeter wafers. The larger wafer diameter is intended to make production more efficient and, in the long term, improve supply for applications including EVs and charging infrastructure.

item.title: Faulty software? Waymo faces potential new recall
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: The US traffic safety authority NHTSA has launched a new investigation into Alphabet's subsidiary Waymo after its driverless taxis repeatedly passed stopped school buses in violation of regulations. An investigation is now exploring why a software update rolled out at the end of 2025 failed to prevent these dangerous violations.

item.title: Kia reveals UK prices for PV5 Chassis and high-roof electric van
item.dc:creator: Ciaran Daly
item.description: Two new additions to Kia's PV5 electric van range, the Chassis and the high-roof Cargo L2/H2, are expected to be available from £25,605 and £27,355 respectively - once they qualify for the UK's Zero Emission Van Grant (ZEVG). Both models are now available to order, with first deliveries of the Chassis expected in Q1 2027.

item.title: Xpeng launches range-extender SUVs in 11 Middle Eastern and African markets
item.dc:creator: Ciaran Daly
item.description: Xpeng has opened pre-orders for its flagship GX and G9L SUVs in 11 countries across the MEA region. The two models are being introduced in a shared launch across ten markets, with the GX also launching in Egypt and the G9L in Ghana.

item.title: Pulsa to open private wallboxes for EV drivers
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: With Pulsa, private wallboxes can be temporarily made accessible to other EV drivers. Three weeks after its launch, the platform has reported 250 registrations.

item.title: Volvo Penta and Ammann develop all-electric road paver
item.dc:creator: Florian Treiss
item.description: Swiss construction machinery manufacturer Ammann, together with drive specialist Volvo Penta, has developed a fully electric road paver. The eABG 4820 is designed to combine the performance of conventional diesel machines with locally emission-free operation.

item.title: CATL explores lithium-air batteries as a long-term research focus
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: CATL is considering lithium-air batteries as a long-term research option. The technology theoretically promises a significantly higher energy density than today's lithium-ion batteries. However, it is still far from market-ready vehicle batteries or a range of 2,000 km.

item.title: Polestar’s design strategy: Formula 2030 showcar sets the direction
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: Polestar unveils the Formula 2030 concept car, showcasing the brand's future design direction. Formula 2030 is the first study under the leadership of Chief Designer Philipp Römers, who took up the position in mid-2024. As a four-door sports car, the show car is intended to emphasize that performance remains at the heart of the brand.

item.title: BYD considers building a battery factory in Portugal
item.dc:creator: Florian Treiss
item.description: BYD is reportedly considering building a battery factory in Portugal - potentially at the former Galp refinery in Matosinhos near Porto. It remains unclear whether battery cells or complete battery systems would be manufactured there. Such a battery factory would align well with a potential BYD car factory in Spain.

item.title: VW hints at SSP model production at Martorell Seat plant
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: In an internal report on future collective bargaining strategy, Volkswagen has also indicated that it will "probably assign a platform and products" to the Seat plant in Martorell (Spain). This could refer to the SSP, which will underpin the electric successors to the Cupra Leon and Formentor.
